title: EPUB Chapters Open, but the Table of Contents Is Missing: What to Check
primary_question: Why can I read every chapter of an EPUB while one reading app shows an empty or incomplete table of contents, and how can I diagnose the actual cause safely?
source_title: Check an EPUB’s Table of Contents and Chapter Order

fact_sources.supports: W3C EPUB 3.3 Recommendation (2026-01-13) requires exactly one EPUB navigation document identified in the package manifest by the nav property; its navigation document contains exactly one toc nav; the spine provides a separate reading sequence. Inspected relevant sections 5.6.2.2, 7.2 and 7.4.2.

W3C EPUB Reading Systems 3.3 Recommendation section 7 states EPUB 3 readers must process navigation documents and expose toc nav links and headings regardless of whether the navigation document is in the spine; it does not prescribe a particular menu design.

Official W3C EPUBCheck user documentation describes the packaged-file command epubcheck filename.epub and interpretation of errors and warnings; conformance checks do not replace editorial comparison of expected chapter entries.

new_examples: An invented twelve-section field handbook is exported twice; a desktop reader imports revision B and the phone retains revision A. A version/file-identity comparison and controlled reimport explain the difference without automatically blaming reader implementation.

An invented community cookbook's chapters remain reachable through its spine, but its generated navigation menu lists only the introduction. Inspection of toc entries separates content availability from navigation completeness and motivates a reproducible source/export correction.
editorial_notes: Written independently on 2026-11-20 for the narrow search problem of an EPUB reading app's missing generated TOC while chapters remain readable; distinct from the canonical ONNELLAB checklist for comparing expected contents and chapter order. Reviewed official W3C EPUB 3.3, EPUB Reading Systems 3.3 and W3C EPUBCheck command guide; all three HTTPS fact references plus the exact canonical source URL returned HTTP 200 from the Mac in this run. Read the full canonical Markdown file and kept a separate question, research-specific diagnosis, and two entirely fictional newly authored examples. The article does not claim actual device test results, and preserves EPUB originals/annotations. No images, external prose passages, secrets or third-party artwork were copied. Proofread for English grammar, structure, scope, rights and non-universal claims; the executable package example is explicitly conditional on an EPUBCheck installation. This brief's source_url is the verified official article URL, not a claim that the Blogger article was syndicated verbatim.
